ch02.before: The Special Branch was organized into three sections

ch02.caption: Pan Hannian, born 1906, a native of Yixing, Jiangsu. He joined the Chinese Communist Party in 1925, moved to the hidden front in April 1931 as chief of the Central Special Branch's Second Section, and from the latter half of 1932 directed the work of the Central Special Branch.

ch02.before: The First Section of the Central Special Branch was the earliest

ch02.caption: Zhao Rong, that is, Kang Sheng, born 1898, a native of Zhucheng, Shandong. He joined the Chinese Communist Party in 1925, and after 1931 served as head of the CCP Central Organization Department, a member of the provisional Political Bureau, and chief of the Central Special Branch's Third Section; from early 1932 he directed the work of the Central Special Branch.

ch02.caption: Bao Junfu, born 1901, a native of Zhongshan county, Guangdong. After becoming our Party's first important double-agent relationship, he played an important part in protecting the safety of the Party's central organs.

ch02.before: That March, Chen Lifu, Zhang Daofan, Yang Jianhong
ch02.alt: A studio portrait of a young man in a peaked, military-style cap and high-collared uniform.
ch02.caption: Chen Lifu, born 1900, a native of Huzhou, Zhejiang. In February 1928 the Kuomintang Central Standing Committee named Chiang Kai-shek concurrent head of the Organization Department; on Chen Guofu's advice Chiang set up a separate Investigation Section to monitor, investigate, and strike at rival parties, and Chen Lifu thereby became its first chief.

ch02.caption: When Bao Junfu served as the Investigation Section's Shanghai special commissioner, he set up his office in an over-the-street building like this one, said to have stood opposite Dade Lane on North Sichuan Road (today's Sichuan North Road) in Shanghai.

ch02.caption: Xu Enzeng, born 1898, a native of Huzhou, Zhejiang. In his youth he studied electrical engineering in the United States, and later directed the Kuomintang's investigation work for as long as fourteen years.

ch02.before: Afterward Huang Molan received Pan Hannian's instruction
ch02.alt: A studio portrait of a young woman with bobbed hair in a patterned qipao.
ch02.caption: Huang Molan, born 1907, joined the Party in 1926. From late 1928 she served as a secretary of the Central Secretariat and as a confidential courier; in January 1931 she took charge of external liaison and established a single-line link with Pan Hannian.

ch03.alt: Eleven men in long gowns and military uniforms stand in a row on open ground before a large earthen mound, the tomb rising behind them.
ch03.caption: In the summer of 1936, with North China in crisis, Chiang Kai-shek set the outside threat aside for the civil war; in October he came to Xi'an himself to force Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng to attack the Red Army in northern Shaanxi. Here Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng accompany Chiang Kai-shek on a visit to Maoling, the tomb of Emperor Wu of Han, in Xingping County. Third from the right is Yang Hucheng, sixth Zhang Xueliang, seventh Chiang Kai-shek, tenth Feng Qinzai, eleventh Shao Lizi. (The caption is the source's own.)
